notes.content: [h3]🔹 Item Optimization[/h3][list][*][p]Items of the same type are now [b]combined into one[/b] instead of spawning separately.[/p][/*][*][p]Their [b]values are added together[/b], so the player only needs to pick up one.[/p][/*][*][p]This greatly reduces the number of items on screen and lowers [b]CPU usage[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45557759/795538d9e94a312426f2d015b20461bf5166e660.gif"][/img][/p][h3]🔹 Region Loading[/h3][list][*][p]Implemented a new [b]region-based loading system[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Only the areas around the player are fully loaded, reducing the load on the [b]GPU[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Expect better performance, especially in larger maps.[/p][/*][/list][h3]🔹 Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]General bug fixes and stability improvements.[/p][/*][*][p]Minor polish to improve overall gameplay experience.[/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you for all your feedback and support! 🙏 Every update brings us closer to making the game run smoother for everyone.[/p]

notes.title: New Passive defense Skills
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

We’re back with another core systems update for our evolving skill system!

What’s New?
Until now, we’ve introduced the Attack and Damage skill branches — giving you offensive power to take down enemies more efficiently.
Now it’s time to protect yourself.

Defense Skills:
New passive abilities that reduce the incoming damage you take. Whether you're facing hordes or bosses, staying alive just got a lot more strategic.

Life Skills:
We’ve also added health-boosting skills to help you survive longer in the battlefield. These new passives increase your maximum life and resilience.

What's Next?
We’re continuing to expand the skill system and gameplay depth with every update. This version lays the groundwork for build diversity and more tactical progression in future encounters.

Thanks for playing, and as always, let us know what you think!
More updates soon!

— The Dev Team

notes.title: DevLog - Creating Dynamic Shaders for Attack Areas version 0.0.0.7
notes.content:
During the development of our combat system, I noticed that the visual feedback for attack areas needed to be more impactful. Initially, we were using a simple red cone texture to represent the affected area — functional, but not visually impressive.

I decided to evolve the system by creating custom shaders to bring the attack areas to life, making them more dynamic and responsive.

Goal
The goal was to create a visual effect that conveyed the attack charging process:

Start softly and grow stronger over time.

Visually expand progressively.

Transition colors during the attack charge.

Apply fade out effects on the edges for a smoother integration with the environment.

First Version
The first shader we developed was for the attack cone:

The radius would grow over time as the attack charged.

It had a radial gradient filling from the center outward.

It automatically responded to the object's activation in the game (no need to instantiate a new material).

While functional, the visual still felt rigid. There was no color transition or edge fading vertically.

Improvements Implemented
We refined the shader by adding:

Color interpolation between a start color and an end color during the charge time (ColorStart → ColorEnd).

Maximum opacity control to allow for more "ethereal" or solid effects depending on the situation.

Fade out on the Y-axis borders, to soften the top and bottom edges of the cone, making it blend better with the environment.

These changes made the attacks feel much more alive, giving the impression of energy building up before release.

Expanding to Other Attack Types
With the cone shader solidified, we created a second shader for linear attacks (like arrows and straight-line spells):

The fill grows horizontally (on the X-axis).

The line advances smoothly from the origin to the maximum range.

We applied the same principles of color gradient and edge fading.

This way, we could reuse the same visual logic across different types of attacks, maintaining artistic consistency throughout the game.

Technical Notes
The shaders are fully controlled via material parameters, with no need for new material instances.

The system uses _StartTime to sync the shader animation with the moment the attack is triggered.

Color and opacity effects are parameterized for fine-tuning each skill or ability.

Results
The new attack area system brought a massive improvement in visual clarity and gameplay impact. Now players can better perceive imminent danger and react visually to enemy attacks much more instinctively.

Additionally, the shaders are lightweight, scalable, and easy to maintain.

notes.title: DevLog – Optimizing the Damage Flood
notes.content:
Another round of optimization magic! This time, we’ve tackled the chaotic mess that was our damage number system. Let me explain what was going down...

We use pop-up numbers to show how much damage each enemy takes. But once we introduced floor-based damage skills — like fire zones — we had a LOT of little numbers flying around.

Especially by Wave 6, when the screen’s packed with enemies and fire, the game started lagging. Turns out, most of the damage being displayed was just 1... over and over again... endlessly.

So we changed how it works: now each enemy tracks the damage they receive, and only shows a pop-up when they’ve taken 10 or more in total. It’s way smoother and easier on the FPS.

The result? Fewer draw calls, better performance, and a much cleaner battlefield. Optimization wins again!

Thanks for playing Eternal Survival! Wishlist, buy it, or better yet — join our community and help shape the future of this game!

notes.title: Great Update 0.0.0.4
notes.content:
Attention, adventurers! Today’s patch is packed with sizzling new features fresh out of the oven! Get ready for a fiery adventure!

Update 1: Scorching Fire Zones
Fireballs now leave behind blazing hot areas that deal 30% of the fireball's total damage while you're standing in them. It’s like a burn buffet – the more you dance, the more you roast!

Update 2: Lingering Burns
If an enemy (or brave player) dares to walk through these fiery zones, they’ll leave scorched and burning for a while. Escaping the fire isn’t enough – you might still end up as a tasty barbecue skewer!

Update 3: Upgraded Basic Attack
Our mage’s basic attack used to hit only one target, but not anymore! Now, it pierces through enemies, and with every new level, you’ll hit one more target. That’s right – each level means a new guest at your fireball party!

Update 4: The Exploding Fairy!
Every 2 seconds, a cute little fairy spawns and dances around you. But don’t let her sweetness fool you – when an enemy gets close… BOOM! She flies at them and explodes, creating a fiery area that sets everything ablaze – in the most adorable way possible!

Update 5: Visual Optimization
We’ve made a huge step in performance: the environment is now baked into a single image, drastically reducing draw calls. That means the game runs smoother than a bunny hopping through a carrot patch!

So get ready to burn enemies and have an absolute blast! And remember: in our adventure, fire is your best friend… just don’t get too toasty. Let’s go, warriors – time to dive into the flame-fueled fun! 🚀

notes.title: April 16 Patch - Fixes
notes.content:
Let's go, people! 

Yes, we're back with another patch! This update will be live tomorrow (April 16, 2025), and guess what? You asked for it — we made it happen!

Some folks from the community requested an indicator for firing skills — and boom, it’s in the game now! 

We’ve also fixed some audio bugs, like the music not starting or stopping in the middle of a run. At least… we think we fixed it. 

Next up, we added a brand-new cursor and changed the ambient sound. The old one had a cave vibe — which made sense back when the map was actually a cave. But not anymore!

The pause menu now pauses the game.... Yes I know......

And finally — yep, this one’s spicy — we updated the Fireball skill. Now it creates a fiery area where it hits the enemy. But watch out! If you step into it, you might end up as the BBQ! 

That’s it for this update! Remember, we’re aiming to bring you something new every day this week. And don’t forget to check out our roadmap… even though it's not really a roadmap.
